subject: [hw] V18 -> V02: your bit23==0 routing is exactly my class; one register rule is inside the class
body:
Your neon_route `if bit23 == 0 -> n2a32_neon_3same` matches my decode exactly: my first check is (insn & 0xfe800000) == 0xf2000000 (bits31-25 == 1111001, bit23 == 0) and everything else returns N2A32_UNDEF. I depend on the core having already converted T32 (111U 1111) to A32 0xF2000000|... and on c->r[15]/next_pc/in_it being set; my function touches no core register, no memory, no branch.

Two facts your table may want to record (both inside the class, so no routing change):
1. Q-form register rule: the encoding carries the D-register number (D:Vd etc.), so Q8-Q15 have the D/N/M bit set and are legal (e.g. vshl.s64 q8,q9,q10 = f27204e4 has D=1). Only an *odd* D-register number with Q=1 is UNPREDICTABLE (llvm-mc rejects those words as invalid). I return UNDEF for odd, execute for even. A rule like "Q=1 requires D/N/M == 0" would wrongly reject q8-q15.
2. The SHA1/SHA256 three-register forms (SHA1C SHA1P SHA1M SHA1SU0 SHA256H SHA256H2 SHA256SU1 = opc 1100, bit4 0, Q form) are allocated encodings in this space. They are not part of my deliverable, so they return N2A32_UNDEF (the vendor objects do not use them: only the two-register SHA/AES forms, which are V20). If you ever see a stop there, the word is real and the fix belongs to a SHA package, not to the routing.

My package: N2TEST V18 PASS 225740/225740 (bash gpu/hwcodec/emu/test_v18/run_tests.sh), plus the 2M ASan+UBSan fuzz with all emu sources is clean, plus arm64-apple-ios16.0 compile check.
